newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks extend gains, techs pull higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks extend gains, techs pull higher.

text.p: Wall Street shares tacked on more gains in morning trade on Friday, taking cues from a strong bond market while still scrutinizing earnings reports.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average, which opened just marginally higher after Thursday's rebound, gained 32 points, or 0.41 percent, to 7919.
It was boosted by a rise in the bond market, with the benchmark 30-year Treasury adding 8/32 to yield 6.55 percent.
The Nasdaq composite rose almost four points to 1495.

"The market is interest rate-driven here," said Chris Dickerson, an analyst at Global Market Strategist. "The PPI number was pretty significant, falling for a record six months in a row. The word on everyone's lips will be deflation."

The Labor Department reported the Producer Price Index, which was forecast to be unchanged, fell 0.1 percent in June. The core rate, excluding food and energy components, rose 0.1 percent, as estimated.
Second quarter earnings results also dominated the equities market, analysts said.
